:::{#exm-mahalanobis-eigen}
#### Elliptical contours of a bivariate normal density

Let $\vecf{\mean} = \vzero$ and
$\matr{\covmat} = \pmat{2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2}$,
which has eigenvalues $3$ and $1$,
with eigenvectors $\vecf{q}_1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tp{(1, 1)}$
and $\vecf{q}_2 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tp{(1, -1)}$
([an eigendecomposition example](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#exm-spectral)).
By @thm-mahalanobis-eigen:

$$
\mahal(\vx)^2 = \frac{(x_1 + x_2)^2}{2 \cd 3} + \frac{(x_1 - x_2)^2}{2 \cd 1}
$$

The point

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vx &= \sqrt{3}\,\vecf{q}_1 \\
&= \sqrt{3/2}\,\tp{(1, 1)}
\end{aligned}
$$

has $x_1 + x_2 = \sqrt{6}$ and $x_1 - x_2 = 0$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mahal(\vx)^2 &= 6/6 \\
&= 1;
\end{aligned}
$$

the point $\vx = \vecf{q}_2$
has $x_1 + x_2 = 0$ and $x_1 - x_2 = \sqrt{2}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mahal(\vx)^2 &= 2/2 \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

So the contour $\mahal(\vx) = 1$ of the $\Normal_2\paren{\vzero, \matr{\covmat}}$ density
is an ellipse stretched along $\tp{(1, 1)}$, with half-length $\sqrt{3}$,
and squeezed along $\tp{(1, -1)}$, with half-length $1$:
$X_1$ and $X_2$ are positively correlated (@fig-mahalanobis-eigen).

```{r}
#| label: mahalanobis-eigen-alt
#| echo: false
# The alt text, saved once for the figure and its interactive widget.
fig_alt_mahal_eigen <- paste(
  "Contour plot of the Mahalanobis distance for a bivariate normal density",
  "with variances 2 and covariance 1, in the plane of x1 and x2.",
  "The contours at distances 1 and 2 are nested ellipses",
  "stretched along the line x2 = x1 and squeezed along the line x2 = -x1.",
  "Two dots on the inner ellipse mark the points",
  "that are the square root of 3 along (1, 1) over the square root of 2",
  "and 1 along (1, -1) over the square root of 2."
)
```

:::{#fig-mahalanobis-eigen}

```{r}
#| label: mahalanobis-eigen-plot
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt_mahal_eigen
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 5
library(ggplot2)

# The covariance matrix of the example and its eigendecomposition.
covmat <- matrix(c(2, 1, 1, 2), nrow = 2)
eig <- eigen(covmat)
stopifnot(all.equal(eig$values, c(3, 1)))

# The Mahalanobis distance of each grid point from the mean zero.
grid <- expand.grid(
  x1 = seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 200),
  x2 = seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 200)
)
grid_matrix <- as.matrix(grid)
grid$mahal <- sqrt(rowSums((grid_matrix %*% solve(covmat)) * grid_matrix))

# The points of the example: sqrt(3) q1 and q2, each at distance 1.
q1 <- c(1, 1) / sqrt(2)
q2 <- c(1, -1) / sqrt(2)
examples <- data.frame(
  x1 = c(sqrt(3) * q1[1], q2[1]),
  x2 = c(sqrt(3) * q1[2], q2[2])
)

mahal_plot <- ggplot(grid) +
  aes(x1, x2) +
  geom_contour(
    aes(z = mahal, colour = factor(after_stat(level))),
    breaks = c(1, 2)
  ) +
  geom_point(data = examples, size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Mahalanobis distance", end = 0.7) +
  coord_fixed(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "x1", y = "x2") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  htmltools::div(
    role = "img",
    `aria-label` = fig_alt_mahal_eigen,
    plotly::ggplotly(mahal_plot) |>
      plotly::layout(
        legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.5, xanchor = "center", y = -0.25)
      ) |>
      plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
  )
} else {
  mahal_plot
}
```

The contours of the Mahalanobis distance at $1$ and $2$ for the example.
The dots are the points $\sqrt{3}\,\vecf{q}_1$ and $\vecf{q}_2$ of the example on the inner ellipse.
